summary: example for sense 2b in Infectum (PrS 10/35)

data.turoyo: Yatiwi, mkayaffe. Omər: “Qum,” – məlle li kačke – “qum d əzzan.” Əmmo: “Layko?” Omər: “Mawbannəx.” Əmmo: “Lo kəṯyono hu d saymət ʕam i aṯtayo.” Omər: “Gmalḥaqina.” Əmmo: “Xayr.”
data.translation: Darauf sassen sie fröhlich beisammen. Kander aber sagte zu dem Mädchen; »Auf, wir wollen fortgehen!« »Wohin?« fragte sie. »Ich will dich mitnehmen«, antwortete er. »Ich gehe nicht mit, bis du dich zu mir gelegt hast«. »Wir werden später schon noch dazu kommen«. »Nein«, entgegnete sie.

rationale: New constructional Infectum cell: understood action deferred by Gmalḥaqina; retain the dialogue needed to identify it.

summary: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (PrS 47/59)

data.turoyo: Ummo: "Izox bu ṭuro, ka ḥzelox Gənǧ Xalil aġa w Ḥasan, mar: "Alo, mahzamle l Ḥaǧi Badran aġa Torən ʕAyšane w i məḥafa, alḥequnne.""
data.translation: »Geh in's Gebirge, wenn du Gändsch-Chalîl-Agha und Ḥassan findest, so sage ihnen: Warhaftig, Ḥadschi-Bedrân-Agha hat Tôren-'Aischane und den Baldachin geraubt, eilt ihnen nach.«

rationale: Fill III.2 Imperativ: pursue plural targets with object suffix.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (29/421)

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (30/134)

data.translation: Als er so gesprochen hatte, ritten ihm einige Reiter nach, um ihn zurückzuholen, wegen der Genugtuung, die er ihnen verschafft, und der edlen tat, die er für sie getan hatte. Sie holten ihn aber nicht ein.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit (67/98)

data.turoyo: Koṯən a tre aḥunonayḏe, ʕaṣriye kosoyəm ḥšamto, heš lo malḥaqle, lo bašilo, kəmḥayḏ̣ər i ḥšamtaṯṯe, kəxli.
data.translation: Am Abend kommen seine beiden Brüder; er macht ihnen Abendbrat; ehe er es geschafft hat, ehe es noch gar geworden ist, kommen sie. Er macht ihnen das Abendbrat zurecht, sie essen.

summary: III.1 contrasts caused arrival (theme plus goal) with reflexive ruḥa arrival, while III.2 covers catching, joining and reaching with l- or direct targets. Near-identical 65/408–409 alternates reflexive and non-reflexive descriptions; preserve existing sense numbers despite overlap.
III.3 expectation is predominantly negated lo malḥaq- plus a time clause in these excerpts. Preserve the edition's kaum erwarten rather than recoding as spatial failure.
The event-attainment subsense 2b has an understood task in PrS 10/35 and 67/98. Its exact time constraint is interpretive; no unseen complement or finite form has been reconstructed.

42/6: hawi lḥiqoyo l ḥzaytayḏux clearly describes longing to see someone. Only this lexical form is supplied; a verbal I stem and Part act. classification remain unproved. Lookup search lḥiq returned no matching entry material.
Preterit appears in future conditions at 70/131 and a hypothetical sequence at 56/10. Translation reorders catch/kill at 56/10, so the German order does not determine morphology.
Searches malḥəq ruḥ and malḥaq ruḥ found only the already represented reflexive construction; it remains in III.1 rather than becoming a duplicate idiom.
All 18 occurrence analyses checked. The round 1 corrections and 2b task-attainment proposal are retained; only 1b and 2c are new this round.

New temporal 2c is supported across shop-opening, historical practices and building construction, usually next to ḥze. This is having overlapped an earlier time, not necessarily waiting eagerly for a future event (III.3), nor mere action completion (2b).

Caused arrival III.1 permits supplied goods and communicated reports, as it already permits letters/books in round 1. No light-verb idiom is required for clothes, library material or the bridge metaphor.

The existing Preterit and Imperativ counts from round 1 make routine hospital, doctor and transport examples unnecessary. Jan 1.46/2045 malḥəqli ... lə Nṣiwən has a caused person and place goal; English catch me up is awkward, so it is not selected as a superior context.
Infectum-wa malḥəqiwo is a genuine missing box in the cumulative entry. Its economic and migration uses illustrate two existing senses, not two new lexical verbs.
All quoted English is the supplied project machine translation, preserved exactly and never treated as independent sense evidence.

Is lḥiqoyo in 42/6 a lexical adjective or a synchronically verbal form? What, if any, independently attested I base forms exist? Reader's reported dictionary typo cannot be verified from allowed inputs.
Confirm that Gmalḥaqina in PrS 10/35 and heš lo malḥaqle in 67/98 share the proposed event-attainment construction, and whether the latter specifically means finish in time.
Confirm segmentation of JTM 1.6/9 malḥaqna, 57/118 malḥaqlalle, 57/133 malḥeqəlle, 70/130 malḥaqliyo and Talay 2/11 gmalḥaqnanne.
Talay 1/284 malḥaqli does not unambiguously establish an Imperativ from the excerpt. Check its clause structure before filing it as an example.

Hors 2/118 and Talay 1/219, /276 match existing MM 118 and LB 219, 276 passages respectively. Treat them as cross-reference confirmations, not independent boxed examples. 60/279's German also includes verse 280; no continuation is quoted.
At Jan 2.6/1785, is attachment to the barracks legal/administrative incorporation, physical joining, or both? 1b is proposed from this single passage, without a more specific legal gloss.

Does temporal 2c mean having lived in the earlier period, remembering it, or acquiring a skill in any of Jan 2.7/1857 and Jan 2.32/5322? The recurrent ḥze pairing supports witnessing, but skill acquisition should be checked.
Resolve -le in gədmalḥəqinale (Jan 4.I/204): is the reader a goal of material delivery or the direct reached participant? The frame is retained under III.1 without reconstructing a missing object.

summary: Caused arrival accepts human, animal, letter and book themes; goals may be persons, places or an abstract desired outcome. Reflexive ruḥa marks self-directed arrival. These participant differences are already covered.
Goods for families, reported information, cultural books and a metaphorical bridge extend round 1 caused-arrival themes/goals. The grammatical frame is retained.
